notes.heading: Hypothesis Testing Basics
notes.body: Hypothesis testing involves a null hypothesis (H0) and an alternative hypothesis (H1). The null hypothesis claims that nothing is happening, while the alternative suggests a change or effect.

source.quote: Null hypothesis H0: the "nothing is happening" claim (for example, the mean score is 70). - Alternative hypothesis H1: what we suspect instead (the mean is not 70, or is greater than 70

notes.heading: Test Statistic and Significance Level
notes.body: The test statistic measures how far the sample result is from H0 in standard errors. The significance level (alpha) is the predetermined cutoff for making decisions, commonly set at 0.05.

source.quote: Test statistic: how far the sample result is from H0, measured in standard errors. - Significance level alpha: the cutoff we choose before looking at the data, commonly 0.05

notes.heading: Understanding the p-value
notes.body: The p-value indicates the probability of obtaining a result as extreme as the observed one, assuming H0 is true. A decision rule is applied: if p <= alpha, reject H0; if p > alpha, fail to reject H0.

source.quote: The p-value is the probability of getting a result at least as extreme as ours IF H0 is true. - Decision rule: if p <= alpha, reject H0. If p > alpha, fail to reject H0

notes.heading: Errors in Hypothesis Testing
notes.body: Type I error occurs when H0 is rejected when it is true, with a probability equal to alpha. Type II error happens when H0 is not rejected when it is false, with a probability of beta. Power is defined as 1 - beta.

source.quote: Type I error: rejecting H0 when H0 is actually true. Its probability is alpha. - Type II error: failing to reject H0 when H0 is actually false. Its probability is beta

notes.heading: Worked Example: z-test
notes.body: In a z-test example, the claim is that the average exam score is 70. With a sample mean of 74 from 36 students, the calculated z-value is 2.0, leading to a p-value of approximately 0.0455, which allows us to reject H0.

source.quote: Claim: the average exam score is 70. The population standard deviation is sigma = 12 (known). - Sample: n = 36 students, sample mean = 74. - z = (74 - 70) / (12 / sqrt(36)) = 4 / 2 = 2.0

notes.heading: Common Mistakes in Hypothesis Testing
notes.body: Common mistakes include choosing alpha after seeing the p-value, misinterpreting confidence levels, and confusing statistical significance with practical importance.

source.quote: Choosing alpha after seeing the p-value. - Saying "we are 95% sure H0 is false". - Confusing statistical significance with practical importance
